title: The Effects of Inter-Valley Coupling of Dirac Fermions near Four Dimensions
abstract: We analyze the criticality of an Ising Gross-Neveu-Yukawa (GNY) theory of $N_ψ$ Dirac fermion valleys with intra- and inter-valley interactions, using a renormalization-group analysis in $4-ε$ space-time dimensions to one-loop order. The conventional GNY fixed point of decoupled valleys is unstable against inter-valley fluctuations which are naturally present if the symmetry breaking is driven by short-ranged interactions. At the new fixed point, the critical exponents differ from the conventional GNY universality. Most importantly, Lorentz invariance is broken due to interference effects resulting from the relative rotation between valley coordinate frames. In the limit of large $N_ψ$ the critical fixed point with finite inter-valley coupling remains stable but Lorentz invariance is asymptotically restored.
summary: This theoretical work investigates the quantum critical behavior of Dirac fermions in a multi-valley system using a renormalization group approach. It finds that inter-valley interactions stabilize a new critical fixed point, which breaks Lorentz invariance. The results are particularly valuable for understanding quantum criticality in materials with multiple degenerate electronic bands.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the quantum criticality of an Ising Gross-Neveu-Yukawa (GNY) theory describing Dirac fermions with both intra- and inter-valley interactions.
main_result: A new critical fixed point is found where inter-valley coupling is finite, leading to broken Lorentz invariance, although this symmetry is asymptotically restored in the large $N_\psi$ limit.
method: The analysis employs a renormalization-group (RG) technique using an $\epsilon$ expansion in $4-\epsilon$ dimensions, calculated to one-loop order.
model_or_system: The model involves $N_\psi$ Dirac fermion valleys, motivated by topological phase transitions (like the Kitaev model), coupled to Ising order parameter fields ($\phi$ and $\varphi_{i, i+1}$).
key_observables:
Critical exponents, anomalous dimensions ($\eta_\psi, \eta_\phi, \eta_\varphi$), dynamical critical exponent ($z$), and correlation-length exponents ($
u_1, 
u_2$).
important_parameters: The number of valleys ($N_\psi$), the dimension parameter ($\epsilon$), and the coupling constants ($g_\phi, g_\varphi, \lambda$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes short-ranged interactions and is performed to one-loop order in the continuum field theory approximation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Brillouin zone with Dirac valleys, Feynman diagrams for self-energy and vertex corrections, and plots showing the RG flow of couplings and critical exponents as a function of $N_\psi$.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the full action and the RG methodology (integrating out UV modes) to deriving the coupled RG flow equations for couplings and velocities, culminating in the determination of the stable critical fixed point $P_c$ and its large-$N_\psi$ limit.
why_interesting: The study of critical points in interacting fermion systems, especially those exhibiting topological features like Dirac valleys, is central to understanding strongly correlated materials and quantum phase transitions relevant to condensed matter physics.
